questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that ‘In the performance of his/her duties, the Attorney-General for India shall have the right of audience in all the courts in the territory of India’?
questions.solution: Article 76(3) grants the Attorney-General the right of audience in all courts in India. Article 76(1) covers appointment, 76(2) covers duties, and 76(4) covers term/remuneration.

questions.question:
Match the following subject matters with their concerned Articles.
1. Superintendence, direction and control of elections to be Vested in an Election commission. (A) Article 329
2. Power of parliament to make provision with respect to election to legislature. (B) Article 324
3. Bar of interference by courts in electoral matters. (C) Article 327
questions.solution:
• 1 matches with (B) Article 324 (Establishment of EC).
  • 2 matches with (C) Article 327 (Parliamentary power).
  • 3 matches with (A) Article 329 (Bar on court interference).

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India mentions that “there shall be a Public Service Commission for the Union and a Public Service Commission for each State”?
questions.solution: Article 315(1) provides for the establishment of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) and State Public Service Commissions (SPSCs).

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India provides that the Governor appoints the Chief Minister and later, the Chief Minister recommends the appointment of ministers to the Governor?
questions.solution: Article 164 covers the appointment of the Chief Minister by the Governor and other ministers by the Governor on the advice of the CM.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution empowers the Parliament to restrict or abrogate the fundamental rights of the members of the armed forces, paramilitary forces, police forces, etc.?
questions.solution: Article 33 empowers Parliament to modify the application of Fundamental Rights to members of the armed forces, police, etc., to ensure the proper discharge of their duties and maintenance of discipline.

questions.question: As per Article 361 of the Constitution of India, who among the following shall NOT be answerable to any court for the exercise and performance of the powers and duties of his/her office?
questions.solution: Article 361 provides protection to the President and Governors, stating they shall not be answerable to any court for the exercise of their official duties.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding provisions of the Indian Constitution:
A. The Tenth Schedule contains provisions for disqualification of legislators on the ground of defection, introduced by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985.
B. The Ninth Schedule, added by the First Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951, contains laws that are immune from judicial review.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. The Ninth Schedule was designed to protect land reform laws, and the Tenth Schedule was added to prevent political defections (Anti-Defection Law).

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that all the authorities— civil and judicial— in the territory of India shall act in aid of the Supreme Court?
questions.solution: Article 144 mandates that all civil and judicial authorities in India must act in aid of the Supreme Court.

questions.question: Article 149 of the Constitution deals with ___________.
questions.option_1: the qualifications required for the appointment of the CAG
questions.option_2: the duties and powers of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India
questions.option_3: the term of office of the CAG
questions.solution: While Article 148 establishes the office and appointment of the CAG, Article 149 specifically defines the duties and powers of the CAG regarding the accounts of the Union and the States.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about Article 129 of the Constitution of India?
questions.option_1: It provides for the Supreme Court to give advisory opinions to the President.
questions.option_2: It provides for the Supreme Court to be a court of original jurisdiction.
questions.option_3: It provides for the Supreme Court to be a court of record.
questions.option_4: It provides for the Supreme Court to be the highest court of appeal.
questions.solution: Article 129 declares the Supreme Court to be a 'Court of Record' and grants it the power to punish for contempt of itself.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Schedules of the Indian Constitution:
A. The Constitution of India contains 12 Schedules in total.
B. The Eleventh Schedule relates to the Panchayati Raj institutions, while the Twelfth Schedule relates to Municipalities.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. The Indian Constitution originally had 8 schedules, but currently, there are 12. The 11th Schedule (added by the 73rd Amendment) deals with Panchayats, and the 12th Schedule (added by the 74th Amendment) deals with Municipalities.

questions.question: Which Clause of Article 19 of the Indian Constitution guarantees the 'right to move freely throughout the territory of India'?
questions.solution: Article 19(1)(d) guarantees the right to move freely throughout the territory of India. Other sub-clauses include (a) speech and expression, (b) peaceful assembly, and (c) forming associations.

questions.question: Which Articles of the Constitution of India deal with the Union and its territory?
questions.solution: Articles 1 to 4 under Part I of the Constitution deal with the Union and its territory, including the admission or establishment of new states and alteration of areas/boundaries.

questions.question: In India which of the following is a Gandhian principle of Directive Principles of State Policy?
questions.option_4: To provide equal pay for equal work
questions.solution: Article 40, which directs the State to organize village panchayats, is a key Gandhian principle. Other Gandhian principles include the promotion of cottage industries (Art 43) and prohibition of intoxicating drinks (Art 47).

questions.question: Which of the following Articles says that double jeopardy which says that “no person shall be prosecuted or punished for the same offence more than once?
questions.solution: Article 20(2) provides protection against 'Double Jeopardy', ensuring that no person is prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once.

questions.question: Under which Article of the Directive Principles of State Policy, a working woman on maternity leave, must receive all maternity benefits from the employer?
questions.solution: Article 42 mandates the State to make provisions for securing just and humane conditions of work and for maternity relief.

questions.question: 'The state shall endeavour to secure to all workers a living wage and a decent standard of life'. Which of the following is correct about the given statement in the context of India?
questions.option_1: It is mentioned in the 43rd Article of the Constitution.
questions.option_2: It is mentioned in the 44th Article of Constitution.
questions.option_3: This is a Gandhian principle of Directive Principles of State Policy.
questions.option_4: This is a liberal principle of Directive Principles of State Policy.
questions.solution: Article 43 declares that the state shall endeavour to secure a living wage and a decent standard of life for all workers. It is classified under Socialist principles.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Co-operative Societies in the Indian Constitution:
A. The provisions related to Co-operative Societies are given under Articles 243 ZH to 243 ZT.
B. The 97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011 added Article 43-B to the Directive Principles of State Policy, promoting Co-operative Societies.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. The 97th Amendment Act of 2011 gave constitutional status to cooperative societies by adding Article 19(1)(c), Article 43B (DPSP), and Part IXB (Articles 243ZH to 243ZT).

questions.question: The government is bound to ensure observance of social welfare and labour laws enacted to secure for workmen a life compatible with human dignity, under ___________ of the Indian Constitution.
questions.solution: Article 21 (Protection of life and personal liberty) has been interpreted by the judiciary to include the right to live with human dignity and the state's obligation to ensure social welfare laws.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Right to move to the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights:
1. Article 32 of the Indian Constitution provides the right to move the Supreme Court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
2. Article 30 of the Indian Constitution is also related to the Right to move the Supreme Court.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: Statement 1 is correct. Article 32 provides the right to constitutional remedies. Article 30 is about the right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions.

questions.question: Poshan Abhiyaan is a programme to achieve nutritional status of children from 0 to 6 years. Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution provides for raising the nutrition level?
questions.solution: Article 47 makes it the duty of the State to raise the level of nutrition and the standard of living of its people and to improve public health.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution has the idea that 'No child below the age of fourteen years shall be employed to work in any factory or mine or engaged in any other hazardous employment?
questions.solution: Article 24 prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 years in factories, mines, or any other hazardous occupations.

questions.question: KA Najeeb Vs Union of India case deals with violation of rights under_____
questions.solution: The Union of India v. K.A. Najeeb case is related to Article 21, specifically regarding the right to a speedy trial and the granting of bail even under stringent laws like UAPA if rights are violated.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Constitution of India:
A. Provisions of the Union Executive are contained in Part V of the Constitution.
B. Provisions of Fundamental Rights are also contained in Part V.
Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.solution: Statement A is correct. The Union Executive is in Part V. However, Fundamental Rights are contained in Part III, not Part V.

questions.question: Fundamental duties were not placed in Part III of the Indian Constitution because Part III is_________.
questions.solution: Part III (Fundamental Rights) is justiciable, meaning they are enforceable by courts. Fundamental Duties (Part IVA) are non-justiciable and thus kept separate.
